headline: Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang says his jokey posts about the Muse AI assistant were meant to make Meta cool again, and that they helped its growth.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a light story about an executive's social media tactics, built on his own account with no figures.
importance_line: What changed: only an executive's explanation of why he posted memes, which matters to Muse's users and Meta's rivals as a sign of deliberate brand strategy, though the growth effect is his own unquantified claim.
summary: Business Insider reports that Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, said in a recent podcast interview with David Senra that his meme posts about Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, were meant to make Meta "cool again" and "actually made an impact on growth". Business Insider adds that Muse launched on 8 Sep 2026 and reached the top of Apple's app store ten days later, ahead of ChatGPT, but gives no figures for the effect of the posts.
notes: Interview date not stated by Business Insider; the podcast itself was not opened.
